data.title: Use Case
data.tagline: A description of the main interaction and important exceptions between an actor and a system while reaching a goal
data.learningOutcome: You can define the actor, trigger, main interaction, exceptions, and observable results for one goal, then distinguish a use case from a user story, user flow, and test case.
data.description: For an order refund, a use case states eligibility, what the customer submits, how the system responds, and how expired or duplicate requests end. It describes observable behavior without prescribing internal code.

learning.assumes: You can describe a feature goal but may omit system responses and failure outcomes.
learning.outcome: You can define the actor, trigger, main interaction, exceptions, and observable results for one goal, then distinguish a use case from a user story, user flow, and test case.

explanation.title: Center on one actor goal
explanation.text: Name who is trying to achieve what and what triggers the interaction.

explanation.title: Alternate actions and responses
explanation.text: State what the actor does and what the system displays or changes at every step.

explanation.title: Include important exceptions
explanation.text: Explain how expired, incomplete, or duplicate requests end or return to a recoverable state.

data.boundary: A User Story states the user, goal, and reason. A Use Case expands the interaction, a User Flow diagrams paths, and a Test Case checks one rule with specific inputs.

lessonPractice.title: Which option works best as the use case for “a customer requests a refund”?

options.label: The customer submits a reason for an eligible order; the system checks the deadline and shows the result; expired or duplicate requests explain why and what to do next
options.feedback: Correct. It centers on one actor goal and includes the trigger, interaction, system response, successful result, and important exceptions.

options.label: As a customer, I want to request a refund so I can recover the cost of an unwanted item
options.feedback: That is a user story. It states the user, goal, and reason without describing the interaction and exceptions.

options.label: RefundController calls PaymentService and writes the status to the refunds table
options.feedback: That is internal implementation. A use case describes observable behavior without choosing controllers, services, or tables.

data.agentPrompt: Using only the refund rules I provide, write the “customer requests a refund” use case with its actor, trigger, preconditions, customer actions, system responses, successful result, and important exceptions. List missing rules as questions instead of inventing a refund window, and do not expand into controllers, APIs, or database design. Then check that every ending is visible and understandable to the customer.
